Amy: Heads-up — EU1 slot scarcity for gen-2 models during 08:00-10:00 UTC. p99 is drifting above our 700ms SLO. Can we run a quick supply-curve + admit-threshold calc to see short-term mitigations? :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Raj: Got it. Do we have a 15m snapshot (qps, seq len distro, prewarm hit rate)? Link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood/eu1/fleet/overview

Amy: From last 15m: peak_qps=420, p95=260ms, p99=920ms, avg_seq=480 tokens, effective_batch = 1.1 seq/GPU (we're not batching well during low concurrency). Prewarm hit ~75%.

Lee: Baseline throughput estimate for A100-80 at 480 tokens (gen-2 tuning) -> ~1.0 sequences/sec per GPU when KV cache hot and batch ~1.1. If cache cold it falls to ~0.6 seq/sec.

Maria: Quick supply math (ballpark):
```
qps = 420
throughput_gpu = 1.0  # seq/sec (hot-cache estimate)
safety_headroom = 1.3  # target headroom to keep p99 < SLO
required_gpus = ceil((qps * safety_headroom) / throughput_gpu)
# = ceil(420 * 1.3 / 1.0) = ceil(546) = 546 GPUs
```
This matches why p99 is high — fleet currently at ~420 GPUs for these pools.

Raj: If we use admission control to cap accepted qps to 320 (soft deny above), recompute:
```
cap_qps = 320
required_gpus_cap = ceil((cap_qps * safety_headroom) / throughput_gpu)
# = ceil(320 * 1.3 / 1) = 416 GPUs
saved_gpus = 546 - 416 = 130 GPUs
```
130 GPUs shaved from peak load immediately reduces queuing and p99 risk.

Amy: Good. Can we also tradeoff by improving batching slightly? If we push batch to 1.6 seq/GPU via coalescing window, throughput_gpu -> 1.45 seq/sec (est). Recompute:
```
throughput_gpu_batch = 1.45
required_with_batch = ceil((420 * 1.3) / 1.45) = ceil(546 / 1.45) = ceil(376.55) = 377 GPUs
```
So batch+admit is powerful.

Lee: Caveat: cold-start/cold-cache tail matters. Cold fraction ~25% (from prewarm hit). Cold requests add ~0.35s of extra latency and effectively reduce throughput. We should fold that into safety:
```
cold_frac = 0.25
effective_throughput = throughput_gpu * (1 - cold_frac) + throughput_gpu_cold * cold_frac
# if throughput_gpu_cold ~ 0.6, effective_throughput drops ~10-15%
```
That means required_gpus goes up — we need to budget prewarm pool or improve hit rate.

Maria: Cost quickback: assume $3.20/gpu-hour for on-demand A100. 130 GPUs * $3.2/hr = $416/hr saved when capped (ignoring prewarm cost). If we can reach batch improvements to drop from 546->377, that's 169 GPUs less (~$540/hr).

Raj: Proposal: immediate short-term = admission cap at 320 for service window (08:00-10:00) + raise prewarm pool to hit 90% (adds ~20 GPUs) -> net ~110 GPUs saved and p99 likely under SLO. Medium-term = enable 100ms coalesce window for gen-2 route to increase batch to ~1.4.

Amy: Action items:
- Raj: run canary change to admit cap=320 for eu1.gen2 route for 30m, monitor p99 and error rates. (Canary start: +2m)
- Lee: draft autoscaler tweak to consider effective_throughput formula and cold_frac in GPU target calc.
- Maria: open cost-impact ticket with HD: include numbers above and expected savings.

sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-214320-AUTO (eu1 gen2 p99 breach) — tagging on-call. :rotating_light:

Amy: Thanks — please post quick 30m status update in this thread once canary finishes. If p99 stays <700ms after 15m stable, we'll extend policy for the morning window. :white_check_mark:
